title: Your week is a Dunder Mifflin cold open
dek: Nothing has gone catastrophically wrong yet. Twelve questions about the last seven days and which opening scene your life is quietly turning into.

questions.prompt: Monday, 9:04am. The first thing that happens:

options.label: Someone tests the alarm 'for fun'
One small spill becomes a whole-floor incident
A serious moment goes strangely dark
Something's flying around and nobody is in charge
The person doing parkour over the furniture
The quiet architect of a very long prank
The one who didn't read the instructions, and now there's drama
Weirdly philosophical about one small thing

questions.prompt: One sentence and the cold open writes itself.
questions.helper: Fill both gaps. The camera is already on you.
questions.template: I'm the kind of coworker who {a} when {b}.

options.label: prints the fire drill schedule in colour
starts a side quest in the parking lot
turns a nosebleed into a TED talk
brings chili and no receipts
the building is technically on fire
there's free food involved
someone says 'quick favour'
the printer makes a noise

questions.prompt: Pick the scene you'd survive best:

options.label: A pot of something on the carpet
A dummy and a singalong
A jump over a desk
A long silence by some water
Chaotic, but nobody got hurt

One big, visible disaster

questions.prompt: I read the instructions after it breaks.
I'd rather be a legend than be managed.

results.name: The Fire Drill
results.blurb: You don't create drama, you stress-test the building. There's a plan, a timer, and at least one person crying in a stairwell by 10am. You genuinely believe this makes everyone better. It does, eventually, mostly.
strengths: Finds the weak point before it fails
Keeps a cool head in noise
results.watchOut: Not everyone needs the drill. Check whether the room is laughing or hiding.

results.name: The Chili
results.blurb: You had it. It was going well. Then one small, entirely normal movement and now the entire floor is involved, and there's a documentary-level aftermath. You're embarrassed for ten minutes and then weirdly proud of the story.
results.watchOut: Not everything needs to be carried across the room. Use two trips.

results.name: The CPR Dummy
results.blurb: In a genuinely serious moment, your brain offers a joke. Sometimes it's the exact thing that lets everyone breathe. Sometimes it lands like a brick in a silent room. You are never boring, which is both the gift and the hazard.
strengths: Releases tension nobody else will touch
results.watchOut: Humour is a door, not a hiding place. Stay for the sincere part too.

results.name: The Bat
results.blurb: Your week has one moving problem in it and everyone has a different theory about what to do. Nobody is in charge, somebody's under a desk, and you're the one whose solution makes the situation worse in a memorable way.
results.watchOut: Panic spreads faster than solutions. Breathe, then appoint one person.

results.name: The Parkour
results.blurb: You saw a straight line and took it, over the furniture, past the sensible route, into the middle of somebody's meeting. Technically you got there faster. The route remains a talking point, and you'd do it again on Thursday.
results.watchOut: Speed is not the same as progress. Ask if the shortcut is worth the bill.

results.name: The Jell-O Stapler
results.blurb: You are patient in a way that frightens people. You've been planning this for eleven days and nobody suspects a thing, and when it lands the whole office laughs and you look completely innocent. It's affection. It's also a warning.
results.watchOut: Pranks need a landing pad. Make sure the person can laugh at the end.

results.name: The George Foreman Grill
results.blurb: You had a plan, a shortcut and complete confidence. The instructions were right there. Now there's a small incident, a bandage and a story that will follow you for years, and you're still not sure what the manual would have added.
strengths: Bounces back from a bad call
results.watchOut: Read the manual. It takes four minutes and saves a season of jokes.

results.name: The Koi Pond
results.blurb: The thing you're upset about is not the thing everyone else is discussing. You've gone quiet, mildly philosophical, and vaguely unavailable. When you finally explain it, it's a small detail nobody noticed, and it turns out to matter more than the big problem.
strengths: Calm in a way that spreads
results.watchOut: Say the small thing early. Silence makes people guess wrong about you.
